approach.method_basis: The reference is DST, the Differentiable Scaffolding Tree of Fu and colleagues, which makes discrete molecular editing differentiable. A molecule is first rewritten as a tree whose nodes are whole substructures, single atoms and intact rings, rather than individual bonds and atoms. The identity of each terminal node, and whether that node exists at all, is then relaxed from a discrete choice into a continuous probability vector, which turns the tree into a smooth object that can be differentiated. A scoring surrogate reads the relaxed tree and its gradient is followed uphill, shifting probability mass toward the substructures the surrogate believes will raise the score. The optimized probabilities are then sampled back down to a discrete tree, and a real molecule is assembled from that tree by choosing attachment atoms and bond orders. The surrogate itself is in two parts: a graph encoder pretrained on unlabeled molecules by predicting masked-out substructures and frozen thereafter, plus a small linear readout refitted on the objective's own scored observations after every batch of feedback.
approach.novelty: Being a root, its commitments are the concrete form it gives that idea. Published versions of this method assume a surrogate trained on a large pool of already-scored molecules, which is unavailable here, so this node splits the surrogate in two: an encoder learned only from unlabeled structure and frozen, and a small ridge readout carrying all the task-specific signal, refitted from as few as ten labels and updated after each batch. It restricts each optimization to at most two terminal substitutions and two expansion sites and holds the interior of the starting molecule fixed, which guarantees a chemically intact product but also bounds how far any single proposal can travel from where it began. Starting molecules are drawn from the scored archive with an exponential preference for high rank rather than greedily. Twenty-two gradient steps are taken per optimization under one frozen surrogate version, so the target does not move underneath the ascent, and the diversity-selection objective of the original published method is deliberately not imported.

observed_bottleneck: This root has no Parent. Observations n-4fa9546e559e and n-de3f755cf329 establish that graph evolution and learned fragment remasking can generate valid novel structures and reuse accepted feedback, while most evaluated proposals do not exceed their generating molecules. They motivate measuring proposal selectivity, but do not establish a DST-specific failure or the usefulness of gradient uncertainty. The benchmark difficulty addressed here is to extract useful local structural directions from very few task-local scores, and then preserve those directions when continuous identity/existence variables become assembled discrete molecules. A useful unlabeled graph representation, informative small-sample readout, and faithful relaxed-to-discrete transfer are untested prerequisites for this root.
hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained masked-substructure graph encoder, fit a regularized linear readout to current-task accepted scores, ascend that fixed surrogate through relaxed leaf identities and leaf/expansion existence variables of observed molecules' scaffolding trees, and stochastically sample and assemble new structures from the optimized variables while preserving their internal scaffold context.

finding_summary.headline: Mid-field at 0.3619: the structural gradients ran cleanly and pointed the wrong way on average
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now knows that this style of surrogate-gradient construction executes faithfully at this budget, and that the surrogate is systematically optimistic. It is fitted in sample to a few hundred points, it is ascended to a strictly higher prediction every single time, and the molecules assembled from that ascent still average worse than the molecules they were built from. The failure is not in the gradient step, which is verified, but in the two lossy translations after it: from relaxed probabilities to a sampled tree, and from a tree to an assembled molecule, where roughly a quarter of attempts fail outright. At 0.3619 against a field spanning 0.2331 to 0.5103, this sits well clear of the undirected search methods and well short of the leader, which suggests that a learned model of structure is worth having but that a point estimate with no uncertainty is the wrong thing to ascend, since ascent drives proposals precisely into the region where the fit extrapolates worst. What stays open is whether calibrating the readout, with a posterior rather than a point prediction or an explicit penalty for distance from the fitted data, would close the optimism gap, and whether the fixed-interior constraint that keeps the chemistry clean is also what caps the score.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean 0.361872161920233 on the single screening seed, placing this root in the middle of the thirteen-root field. Per objective: 0.5890616392238477, 0.42602011617052177, 0.380138751942517, 0.23408968632790841 and 0.18005061593636776. Every observable activated and the falsifier did not trigger. Masked-substructure pretraining cut held-out loss from 5.444202465850716 to 0.9686623942998355 over 30000 steps, publishing the checkpoint at step 27000. All 150 readout fits used only prior same-objective observations, growing from 10 to 300 records. All 175 structural optimizations ended with a surrogate prediction strictly above their own starting relaxation, with all four gradient families active at every one of the 3850 steps. From 6268 sampled trees, 1450 valid novel context-preserving molecules were assembled; the remainder were 3712 duplicates and 1106 failed assemblies, of which 732 had no compatible attachment point and 374 failed kekulization. The result the run turns on is the transfer gap: 380 of 1450 proposals beat their generating source, but the mean actual score change relative to that source was negative on all five objectives, ranging from -0.00180775181701 to -0.108386772041, while the surrogate's relaxed gain was positive throughout. Predicted improvements were realised only 26 to 46 percent of the time, and chronological prediction error reached 0.135969779 on the worst objective against an in-sample residual of 0.0515970171356 on the same one.

molecular.headline: Clean, fully ring-bearing drug-like chemistry that never leaves the scaffolds it was handed
molecular.overall_character: This is the most chemically respectable output of the three nodes examined. Every single proposal on every objective contains a ring closure and essentially all contain aromatic atoms, with a ring closure rate of 1.0 and aromatic rate of 0.986 to 1.0 across the five sets, no cumulated double bonds anywhere, and molecules of ordinary size at mean SMILES lengths of 41 to 80. The recurring pieces are real medicinal chemistry: quinolines, indoles, oxadiazoles, tetrazoles, piperazines, morpholines, pyrimidines and aryl amides. The cost of that cleanliness is visible in the same molecules. Because the interior of the starting structure is held fixed and only terminal units are edited, each objective's whole trajectory orbits the scaffolds present in the ten supplied starting molecules, so the top-scoring sets read as decoration series rather than as searches. Stereocentres are absent throughout, and a recurring set of reagent-grade functional groups shows the substructure alphabet carries no notion of stability.

per_task.generated_character: A single elaborated core: a methylated pyrimidinedione fused to a pyrrole, N-linked to a benzoate ester and carrying an oxadiazolyl ether, decorated with pyridines, pyrimidines and thiophenes. It is a direct elaboration of one of the supplied starting molecules.
liabilities: an anionic phenolate carried as a scoring feature inside the top-scoring entries
formaldehyde-acetal OCO fragments appearing in the low-scoring entries
densely fused biaryl-on-biaryl decoration pushing molecules past 100 SMILES characters
missing_features: a scaffold hop away from the elaborated core, which the fixed-interior rule forbids by construction
saturated linkers that would break the near-planar all-aromatic character of the whole series
defined stereochemistry at the few sp3 centres the series does contain
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The whole top twelve sits in a 0.003 band from 0.5863 to 0.5890616392238477 against a starting best of 0.548381482770623, so the gradient is genuinely being followed but into an extremely flat region. What separates the top from the 0.534 to 0.540 bottom is the oxadiazole ether and the N-aryl substitution; the low entries are the plain methoxy-indole carboxanilide with only small oxygen decorations.

per_task.generated_character: A dichlorophenyl sulfenamide on a proline-like pyrrolidine, joined through an aminal carbon to a morpholine or thiomorpholine and to a biaryl aniline. The halogen rate on this objective is 0.9828, so essentially every molecule carries chlorine or bromine.
liabilities: acid chlorides carried through most of the top twelve, which are reagents rather than compounds
sulfenamide S-N bonds as the load-bearing feature of the entire top-scoring family
aminal carbons bearing two nitrogens, which are hydrolytically unstable
a fluoromethyl ether decoration appearing on the highest-scoring entries
missing_features: a stable connectivity that reproduces whatever the S-N linkage is contributing to the score
an ordinary secondary or tertiary amine of the kind this target class rewards, in place of the aminal
defined stereochemistry, though the pyrrolidine and benzylic centres here are real stereocentres
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The single largest jump in the set comes from adding one thiol to the dichlorophenyl ring, taking 0.38644405836045415 to 0.42602011617052177. Across the top twelve the pattern is aryl halide plus S-N linkage plus a basic saturated amine ring. The lowest entries are the sulfonamide versions of the same molecules, which is telling: replacing the S-N sulfenamide with a proper sulfonamide costs more than an order of magnitude.

per_task.generated_character: A 4,5-dihydropyrazole bearing a furyloxy-phenyl group and an aminomethyl link to a pyridine or pyrimidine. Compact molecules at a mean SMILES length of 41.4, all ring-bearing and all containing aromatic atoms.
liabilities: free thiol and free aryl iodide substituents introduced as terminal decorations
a bare phosphorus substituent on nitrogen in one of the final proposals
an N-Cl bond appearing in another of the final proposals
one top-scoring entry carries a cumulated allene, which is not a stable substituent
missing_features: polar solubilising groups anywhere on the scaffold, absent from the entire series
an aromatic five-membered ring in place of the partially saturated pyrazoline core
defined stereochemistry at the pyrazoline sp3 carbon, which is a genuine stereocentre
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The furan-2-yloxy phenyl on the pyrazoline is fixed across the entire top twelve, so the whole gradient runs through the small amine cap: a pyridyl aminomethyl reaches 0.377 to 0.380 while a piperidine, morpholine or plain phenyl cap on the identical scaffold collapses to 1e-5 or below. That is an unusually sharp cliff for a single-group change, and the search found the right side of it early and then stopped moving.

per_task.generated_character: A tight decoration series on one supplied starting molecule: a methylquinoline benzyl ether linked to the anilide of an N-methylpiperidine carboxamide, with an added imidazolidine ring on the aniline. Every top entry shares that exact skeleton.
liabilities: an aliphatic aldehyde as the highest-scoring terminal group, reactive and metabolically labile
N-hydroxy piperidines appearing in the low-scoring entries
methylthio ether decorations appearing on the late proposals
missing_features: a second scaffold family, which the fixed-interior constraint prevents this generator from reaching
carboxylic acid or other strongly polar termini, absent from the entire series
defined stereochemistry at the two substituted piperidine ring carbons
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top twelve span 0.1749 to 0.18005061593636776, a 0.005 band, and the best is only 0.013 above the best supplied starting molecule at 0.1678386594791329. What moves the score is the small terminal group on the piperidine, aldehyde or acetyl or primary amide, together with the added imidazolidine on the aniline; entries lacking that added ring sit at 0.118.

per_task.generated_character: Methoxy-indole carboxamides derived from a supplied starting molecule, decorated with aziridinyloxy groups, fluorines and small azoles. The score span is extreme, best 0.23408968632790841 against a median of 9e-06, so the overwhelming majority of proposals are effectively zero.
liabilities: a trimethylsilyl group on nitrogen in the single best-scoring molecule, not a medicinal chemistry substituent
N-O aziridine ethers recurring through the top-scoring entries
peroxide linkages present in every one of the final six proposals
aminal carbons replacing the amide throughout the terminal cohort
missing_features: the fluorinated aryl and fused triazole chemistry this class of objective rewards
an amide or other stable connectivity retained through the late proposals instead of an aminal
defined stereochemistry, which this class of objective is built around
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The single best molecule differs from its neighbours mainly by a trimethylsilyl group on the anilide nitrogen, which reads far more like the objective being gamed than like real signal. Below it, entries that keep the indole-2-carboxamide intact score 0.07 to 0.19; once the amide is replaced by an aminal carbon the scores fall to 1e-13 and below, and that is exactly where the whole final cohort ends up.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every optimization holds the interior of a starting molecule fixed and edits at most two terminal units and two expansion sites, and every objective's top-scoring set is a decoration series on one of the ten supplied starting scaffolds, in one case spanning as little as 0.003 in score across twelve entries.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can only decorate the structures it is given; it cannot originate a core.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A generator built this way is bounded by whatever chemistry it was seeded with, and the cleanliness of its output is bought with that bound. It would need an operation that replaces or rebuilds interior substructure, or a route to assemble a molecule from primitives with no starting structure at all, before it could reach a scaffold nobody handed it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 175 structural optimizations ended above their own starting relaxed prediction, yet the mean actual score change relative to the generating molecule was negative on all five objectives, and predicted improvements were realised only 26 to 46 percent of the time.
transferable_gaps.gap: The learned score model is systematically optimistic about its own edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ascending a point-estimate surrogate fitted to a few hundred labels drives proposals precisely into the region where it extrapolates worst, so the ascent is self-defeating. A generator needs the surrogate to carry uncertainty and to pay a cost for distance from its fitted data, so the ascent stops where the model stops knowing anything.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Of 6268 sampled trees, 1106 failed assembly, 732 of them with no compatible attachment point and 374 failing kekulization, and a further 3712 were duplicates, leaving 1450 usable proposals from all that effort.
transferable_gaps.gap: A quarter of everything the optimizer designs cannot be built into a molecule.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The relaxed representation is not closed under assembly: it can place substructures that the attachment rules then reject. A generator should make attachment compatibility and aromatic ring closure part of the space being optimized, so that gradient effort is never spent on trees that cannot become molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Acid chlorides, sulfenamide S-N bonds, aminal carbons, N-O aziridine ethers, peroxide linkages and a trimethylsilyl group on nitrogen all appear among the highest-scoring molecules, several of them as the load-bearing feature of an entire top-scoring family.
transferable_gaps.gap: Reagent-grade reactive functionality is proposed as if it were finished substituent chemistry.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The substructure alphabet was learned from unlabeled corpus statistics and carries no notion of stability or synthetic accessibility, so an unstable primitive that happens to score gets refitted into the readout and then reinforced. A generator needs those primitives filtered, or the assembled molecule screened, before a proposal is allowed to spend an evaluation and enter the archive it is later fitted on.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across all 1450 proposals on all five objectives, while the emitted molecules routinely contain substituted pyrrolidines, piperidines and pyrazolines whose ring carbons are genuine stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.gap: Configuration is never expressed in any proposal.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The tree representation encodes substructure identity and connectivity but not configuration, so stereochemistry cannot be proposed, optimized or even represented in the relaxation. A generator addressing shape-sensitive properties would need stereo as a variable inside the continuous relaxation, not merely as a tag on the final string.

method_name: DST: gradient-guided construction through relaxed scaffolding trees
method_thesis: Anchor the method in Differentiable Scaffolding Tree: relax molecular substructure identity and existence into continuous variables, ascend a structural surrogate, and sample discrete structures from the optimized variables. [Fu et al., Sections 3.1-3.3](https://wenhao-gao.github.io/assets/publications/2021_DST_ICLR/paper.pdf) describe this proposal mechanism. For our adaptation, derive an atom/ring token alphabet and train a compact graph encoder by masked-substructure reconstruction solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Freeze that encoder and fit a regularized linear scalar readout using only the current objective's accepted observations, updating the readout after feedback. Select scored molecules as local starting structures; hold their internal scaffold context fixed while optimizing relaxed leaf replacement, deletion and expansion variables through the surrogate. Keep surrogate parameters fixed during each structural optimization. Sample edited trees and compatible attachment choices stochastically, assemble new molecules, and repeat generation until the announced batch contains distinct valid structures. The token alphabet supports construction; complete corpus molecules are never retrieved or ranked, and attachment combinations are sampled rather than exhaustively enumerated. Accepted feedback updates both the scored archive and the readout. The hypothesis is that useful structural gradients concentrate new proposals toward real improvements quickly enough to increase the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Reliable gradients from scarce labels and faithful transfer from relaxed to assembled structures are unproven prerequisites.
